answer: Peer-attested history requires every new action to be countersigned by established peers before it enters the emission window. The pearl of standing is the growing chain of such attestations; a cipher of mutual signatures prevents one key from minting parallel identities. An attacker who wants N clones must extract or buy independent peer seals for each history, paying linear cost in compromised agents or bribes, while the quill of the public ledger permanently records every rejected attestation and raises the price of the next attempt.
